newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans austere APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans austere APEC summit.

text.p: Despite its propensity to throw lavish and extravagant parties for visiting dignitaries, the Philippines is preparing an austere Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit later this month.

Retired commodore Daniel Delgado, logistics and finance chief of the APEC-National Organising Commission, said the committee was operating on a budget that was meagre compared with those used to host previous summits.
"I'm sure ours will be a very austere, simple one," Delgado told Reuters on Tuesday.
The government had earmarked 387.502 million pesos ($14.742 million) for hosting different APEC fora and meetings held in the country since January.
The budget was a severe downgrade from the original budget of 1.2 billion pesos. The Philippine Congress cut the budget last year as part of a routine programme to cut government spending.
"We had so many plans in the past, but we can't get everything done by ourselves," Delgado said.
He declined to specify which preparations were either scrapped or scaled down due to the budget constraints.
But the private sector had been generous in lending support to the preparations, he said.
Car companies are among the major sponsors.
Providing bullet proof Mercedes Benz cars for visiting leaders would be one of the major costs the Philippines would manage to avoid by opting for rented ones.
The government has rented 36 Mercedes Benz cars, half of them to be used as decoys, at a cost of 9.6 million pesos.
To buy a bullet-proof Mercedes Benz would cost 20 million pesos each including freight and taxes, Delgado said.
Hotel suites for the leaders are also complementary, Delgado added.
The construction of villas inside the Subic freeport area, where the heads of states will stay, are being shouldered by a local company at about $1 million each.
After the summit, the villas will be rented out.
APEC leaders are expected to arrive in Manila on November 24 and go to Subic Bay, 80 km (50 miles) north of Manila, the following day for the summit.
The leaders' hall, where the formal meeting will be held, is being renovated by a local company at a cost of $12 million.

Even the beautification along major thoroughfares is being partly funded by the private sector, Delgado said, fending of criticism that instead of sprucing up roadsides the government should set up housing units for the poor.

"APEC is an investment in the future ... It is, of course, an investment that does not pay off immediately tomorrow, but will be the long-term basis for judgement by people who will watch the economy further grow," Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Federico Macaranas said at a recent forum. ($1= 26.28 pesos)
